transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Well, I'm here because I've been having this issue where I just... lose chunks of time. I'll be getting ready to leave the house, or sitting down to start work, and I end up spending way too long re-reading emails and texts. Or I'll keep reopening folders on my computer to check them. And I do this thing where I mentally replay conversations over and over. It's like I have to prove to myself that I didn't make some kind of serious mistake. It's really starting to get in the way.
What happens or what do you feel inside if you try to stop yourself from checking or replaying these things?

I'm not exactly sure how to describe it. I just get really agitated. If I try to force myself to stop—like if I just close the email or try to move on to my actual work—I just can't focus. 

It feels like something is wrong or unfinished. My mind just keeps pulling me back to it, and that tense feeling doesn't really go away until I finally just give in and check it again.
Deep down, do you feel that this level of checking makes logical sense, or does it feel excessive and irrational to you?

Oh, I know it's excessive. It really doesn't make logical sense at all. 

Like I mentioned a minute ago, I'm losing whole chunks of time before I can even leave the house or start my work. I work with computers, so I know that reopening the same folders or re-reading the same emails and texts over and over isn't actually accomplishing anything. And mentally replaying those conversations just to prove to myself I didn't make some serious mistake... I know, logically, that I didn't do anything wrong. 

I know it's irrational. But I still get stuck doing it anyway.
How long have you been dealing with these repetitive checking habits and thoughts?

To be honest, I'm really not sure. It's hard to put an exact timeframe on it. 

It feels like it just sort of... crept up on me over time. I can't really point to a specific month or year when it started getting this noticeable or when I started losing so much time to it. I just know it's been happening for a while now, but as for exactly how long... I really couldn't tell you.
On a typical day, roughly how much total time would you say you spend on these checking behaviors and replaying conversations?

I've never really timed it, so I don't have an exact number for you. It's hard to add it all up because it happens in chunks... you know, a bit in the morning before I leave the house, and then off and on while I'm at my computer for work. 

If I had to guess the total time for a whole day... I'm really not sure. I just know it's a lot, and it's enough to get in the way of things, but I couldn't give you a specific amount of hours or anything like that.

Compulsive mental replaying of past conversations to verify no mistakes occurred
Severe tension and agitation when attempting to resist rituals
Awareness that thoughts and rituals are excessive and irrational (preserved insight)
